paper.title: Research status and development prospect of Fe-Mn-C-Al system low-density steels
paper.journal: Journal of Materials Research and Technology
paper.paper_scope: A systematic review of Fe-Mn-C-Al system low-density steels, covering composition design and the role of alloying elements, production/thermal-mechanical processing, strengthening and strain-hardening mechanisms (TRIP, TWIP, MBIP, SIP, DSBR, solution/grain-refinement/precipitation strengthening), microstructure evolution, and service performance (cryogenic performance, impact toughness, fatigue, hydrogen embrittlement, wear and tensile properties).

alloys.description: Low-density Fe-Mn-Al-C steel type whose room-temperature microstructure is δ-ferrite; a high Al content raises the ferrite recrystallization temperature so δ-ferrite grains are hard to refine and elongate into banded morphology along the rolling direction under hot rolling. It has no austenite, so martensite transformation is absent.
alloys.alloys_notes: Constituent phases: δ, B2, DO3, κ. Composition ranges are the classification criteria tabulated for Fe-Mn-Al-C low-density steels; micro-alloying elements (Si, Ni, Cr, V, Mo, Nb, Ti, Cu) may additionally be added to meet service requirements.

source.reason: Table 1 and the text divide Fe-Mn-Al-C low-density steels into four composition types; the single ferrite type is defined by X_Mn<5.0, 5.0<X_Al<12.0, X_C<0.1 (wt.%) and is described as having a δ-ferrite room-temperature microstructure.

alloys.description: Low-density Fe-Mn-Al-C steel type whose room-temperature microstructure consists of equiaxed austenite with annealing twins, because thermal-mechanical processing is located within the single austenite phase region. Deformation mechanism is controlled by stacking fault energy (TRIP/TWIP/MBIP/SIP/DSBR).
alloys.alloys_notes: Constituent phases: γ, α, δ, κ, β-Mn. High C (>0.7 wt%) and Al (>7 wt%) are the primary conditions for κ-carbide formation in single austenite-base steels; Ni/Cu additions may be used and micro-alloying elements are also possible.

source.reason: Table 1 defines the single austenite type by 15.0<X_Mn<30.0, 2.0<X_Al<12.0, 0.5<X_C<2.0 (wt.%), and the text describes its equiaxed austenite plus annealing-twin room-temperature microstructure.

alloys.alloy_name: A-BDP (austenite-base duplex phase) Fe-Mn-Al-C low-density steel
alloys.description: Austenite-base duplex-phase low-density Fe-Mn-Al-C steel; its quenched microstructure is full austenite and, after aging at 500-800 °C, lath-like ferrite forms along austenite grain boundaries with B2 phase within the lath-like ferrite. Complex microstructure includes austenite, α/δ ferrite, B2, DO3, κ-carbide and β-Mn.
alloys.alloys_notes: Constituent phases: α, B2, DO3, γ, κ, β-Mn. Deformation behavior depends strongly on δ-ferrite fraction, hardness difference between austenite and ferrite, and ordered phases in ferrite.

source.reason: Table 1 defines the A-BDP type by 10.0<X_Mn<25.0, 5.0<X_Al<12.0, 0.6<X_C<1.0 (wt.%), and the text describes the A-BDP quenched/aged microstructure evolution.

alloys.alloy_name: F-BDP (ferrite-base duplex phase) Fe-Mn-Al-C low-density steel
alloys.description: Ferrite-base duplex-phase low-density Fe-Mn-Al-C steel; hot-rolled and cold-rolled microstructures are the typical bimodal banded structure of δ-ferrite and austenite, with κ-carbide generated along the austenite/δ-ferrite interface. Ultrafine austenite distributed on the ferrite matrix enables martensite transformation (TRIP) during plastic deformation.
alloys.alloys_notes: Constituent phases: α, δ, B2, DO3, γ, κ, α′. Strain hardening is dominated by the synergistic effect between ferrite plastic deformation and the TRIP effect.

source.reason: Table 1 defines the F-BDP type by 3.0<X_Mn<10.0, 3.0<X_Al<9.0, X_C<0.4 (wt.%), and the text describes the bimodal banded δ-ferrite + austenite microstructure and the role of ultrafine austenite.

processes.process_name: hot rolling + rapid cooling to room temperature
aliases: hot rolling and rapidly cooling to room temperature
processes.description: Forging ingot homogenized at 1100-1250 °C for 1-3 h, then hot-rolled to 2-5 mm thickness between 1100 and 850 °C (with possible reheating between passes), followed by rapid cooling to room temperature. The resulting room-temperature microstructure defines the single ferrite / single austenite / A-BDP / F-BDP classification.
processes.processes_notes: Common to all four Fe-Mn-Al-C steel types; applies across alloys (alloy_id left null). Cooling rate after hot rolling strongly influences intergranular κ-carbide formation.

source.reason: The text states that Fe-Mn-Al-C low-density steels 'after hot rolling and rapidly cooling to room temperature' are divided into single ferrite/austenite, A-BDP and F-BDP steels, and details the homogenization + hot-rolling schedule.

processes.description: Cold rolling (e.g. 30-50% reduction), which generates deformation twins and work hardening, followed by recrystallization annealing to eliminate work hardening, improve toughness and tailor δ-ferrite size, texture and κ-carbide.
processes.processes_notes: Employed for both austenite-base and duplex-phase steels to overcome the coarse lath-like δ-ferrite of the hot-rolled state; applies across alloys (alloy_id left null).

source.reason: The text states 'cold rolling and recrystallization annealing are employed to tailor the δ-ferrite size, texture and κ-carbide (Route 2)', and discusses cold-rolling reduction and annealing time effects.

processes.description: For austenite-base Fe-Mn-C-Al steels, hot-rolled steel is rapidly cooled to room temperature and then subjected to isothermal annealing and aging treatments (Route 1), which is beneficial to the nucleation of nano precipitates and enhances precipitation strengthening.
processes.processes_notes: Can be preceded by cold rolling to increase yield strength while overcoming the strength-ductility trade-off; applies across alloys (alloy_id left null).

source.reason: The text describes that hot-rolled austenite-base steels 'can be rapidly cooled to room temperature and then subjected to isothermal annealing and aging treatments (Route 1)' and that the cold-rolling/annealing/aging combination improves strength.

processes.description: Aging treatment at 500-700 °C for 0.5-2 h to nucleate fine dispersed nano carbides (κ-carbide) and B2 particles in the austenite/ferrite matrix; higher temperature or longer time coarsens intergranular κ*-carbide and forms brittle β-Mn, deteriorating ductility and toughness.
processes.processes_notes: Age hardening tailors carbide precipitation; applies across alloys (alloy_id left null). Precipitate type/size is highly sensitive to annealing/aging temperature and time.

source.reason: The text states 'aging at 500-700 °C for 0.5-2 h (Routes 3 and 4 in Fig. 3) is beneficial to the nucleation of nano precipitates' and describes age-hardening effects on carbides and β-Mn.

processes.description: Solution treatment followed by water quenching, producing a fully austenitic (quenched) matrix; the quenched microstructure of A-BDP steels is full austenite. Subsequent aging at 500-800 °C then forms lath-like ferrite and B2 phases.
processes.processes_notes: Quenching followed by ordering annealing can produce coarse B2 and ultrafine DO3 in ferrite of A-BDP steels; appears as 'Solution-water quenching' in the mechanical-property comparison table; applies across alloys (alloy_id left null).

unmapped_findings: This is a review article; Fe-Mn-C-Al low-density steels are classified into four composition types (single ferrite, single austenite, A-BDP, F-BDP) with quantitative Mn/Al/C ranges given in Table 1 (b0041).
Micro-alloying additions (Si, Ni, Cr, V, Mo, Nb, Ti, Cu) can be made to the Fe-Mn-C-Al system; the role of Si remains controversial and Si is not discussed further (b0016, b0035, b0079).

Key precipitation phases are κ-carbide ((Fe,Mn)3AlC-type, L12 ordered), B2/DO3 ordered phases, β-Mn and MC carbides, whose type/size/distribution control strengthening, strain hardening and service properties (b0068-b0079).
